title: The Most Similar Path in a Graph
summary: Given n cities and m bi-directional roads connecting them, find a path of the same length as the given targetPath with the minimum edit distance.
statement: Given n cities and m bi-directional roads connecting them, find a path of the same length as the given targetPath with the minimum edit distance. Return the sequence of city names in this path, ensuring it is valid and directly connectable. If multiple paths with the minimum edit distance exist, return any one of them. The edit distance is the measure of the differences between the given path and the targetPath.
constraints: Roads are bidirectional and the returned city-index sequence must use one road per consecutive pair.
Minimize positions whose city name differs from target_path; any optimal path is valid. Tests use a deterministic lexicographically smallest optimum when ties occur.
hints: DP by target position and ending city.
For each city, extend only states ending at one of its road neighbors and add one when its name mismatches.
Keep the lowest-cost path per ending city, with deterministic lexicographic tie-breaking.
Every valid path has exactly one prior neighbor state, so the recurrence considers all paths of the required length.
editorial: Every valid path has exactly one prior neighbor state, so the recurrence considers all paths of the required length.

tests.explanation: Path 0,2,4,2 follows roads and has one name mismatch, which is optimal.
Alternating along the only road gives path 0,1,0 with no mismatches.
